commits.message:
fix atomic open_file: set mode via fchmod and close fd on failure

The atomic write branch set the temp file's mode with os.chmod(path),
which follows symlinks: a concurrent writer able to create names in the
destination directory could replace the temp name between open() and
chmod(), redirecting the mode change to an unrelated file. os.fchmod()
operates on the inode that was just created. Additionally, if the mode
call raised, the already-open file descriptor was never closed (leaked).

Set the mode with os.fchmod(fd) where available (falling back to the
path-based chmod on platforms without it, i.e. Windows), and on failure
close the descriptor and remove the temp file before re-raising.

Adds regression tests for the descriptor leak and for the mode being
applied via the fd rather than the symlink-following path.

Closes #3824.

+        # Set the mode on the open fd rather than via the path: os.chmod()
+        # follows symlinks, so a concurrent writer who replaces the temp
+        # name between open() and chmod() could redirect the mode change
+        # to an unrelated file. fchmod() operates on the inode that was
+        # just created (it is unavailable on Windows, where chmod only
+        # toggles the read-only bit and we fall back to the path-based

+            else:
+                os.chmod(tmp_filename, perm)
+        except OSError:
+            os.close(fd)
+            try:
+                os.unlink(tmp_filename)
+            except OSError:

(e.g. --disable-/cache-mode). Wrap usage arguments with
break_on_hyphens=False so options stay intact, adding a matching
parameter to wrap_text (default unchanged for other callers).

+def _make_init_annotate(annotations, cls):
+    """Create a lazy annotation provider for generated initializers.
+
+    On Python 3.14, annotations can be evaluated after a class decorator has
+    run. Generated functions use a private globals dictionary, so evaluating
+    a forward reference there would miss names defined later in the module.
+    Resolve string annotations against the defining module when annotations
+    are requested instead.
+    """
+    module = sys.modules.get(cls.__module__)
+    module_globals = module.__dict__ if module is not None else {}
+    module_name = cls.__module__
+
+    def annotate(format):
+        from annotationlib import Format, ForwardRef
+
+        if format == Format.VALUE:
+            result = {}
+            for name, annotation in annotations.items():
+                if isinstance(annotation, str):
+                    try:
+                        annotation = eval(annotation, module_globals)
+                    except NameError:
+                        annotation = ForwardRef(annotation, module=module_name)
+                result[name] = annotation
+            return result
+
+        if format == Format.FORWARDREF:
+            return {
+                name: (
+                    ForwardRef(annotation, module=module_name)
+                    if isinstance(annotation, str)
+                    else annotation
+                )
+                for name, annotation in annotations.items()
+            }
+
+        if format == Format.STRING:
+            return {
+                name: annotation if isinstance(annotation, str) else repr(annotation)
+                for name, annotation in annotations.items()
+            }
+
+        raise NotImplementedError
+
+    return annotate
+

commits.message:
🚸 Add notes to dependency errors with the function and path operation

When a path operation or one of its dependencies has an invalid parameter
declaration, the error raised at startup only says what's wrong, e.g.
"Path params must be of one of the supported types", without saying in which
function. Nested dependencies are not in the traceback, the call stack only
shows the path operation decorator, so in a large app it's hard to find the
dependency to fix.

Add PEP 678 exception notes while building the dependency graph:

- `get_dependant()` now wraps the previous implementation (`_build_dependant()`)
  and, on error, adds a note with the function being analyzed, its source
  file and line, and the parameter that declared it as a dependency. Each
  level of nested dependencies adds its own note, so the notes show the chain
  from the function with the problem up to the path operation.
- Creating an `APIRoute` or `APIWebSocketRoute` adds a note with the methods
  and path, e.g. "While creating the path operation GET /items/{item_id}".

Example:

    AssertionError: Path params must be of one of the supported types
    While analyzing get_tenant (main.py, line 6), the dependency for the parameter 'tenant'
    While analyzing get_user (main.py, line 10), the dependency for the parameter 'user'
    While analyzing me (main.py, line 14)
    While creating the path operation GET /t/{tenant_id}/me

The exception type, message, traceback, and chaining are unchanged, notes
only add context below the message. Notes are only built when an error is
raised, mainly at startup, so there's no cost otherwise. They include function
names, source locations, parameter names, and route paths, never values.
Python 3.10 has no exception notes, errors there are unchanged.

🚸 Show a request parameter error for invalid parameter types

An unsupported type annotation for a request parameter, e.g. a plain class
used as a query or body parameter, raised the error message meant for response
models: "Invalid args for response field! ... If you are using a return type
annotation ... response_model=None". That points to the wrong place.

`create_model_field()` now uses that message only for response fields, which
are created in serialization mode (response models, additional responses,
stream items). Request parameters and bodies, created in validation mode,
get:

    Invalid type annotation for the request parameter 'item'! Hint: check that
    <class 'main.Item'> is a valid Pydantic field type. Read more:
    https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/extra-data-types/

The exception type (`FastAPIError`) is unchanged, and so is the message for
response models.

fix_message: Handle deferred unittest subtest reports in JUnit regressions

commits.message:
Report subtests as separate JUnit XML testcases

Keep subtest reports out of the parent reporter cache and retain parent outcomes and inclusive durations. Include repeated contexts, unittest, teardown errors, output, and xdist regression coverage.

Refs #13876.

Co-authored-by: Codex <codex@openai.com>
commits.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+JUnit XML reports now include a separate testcase for every subtest, with distinct names for repeated contexts, alongside the parent test.
@@ -642,6 +642,20 @@ instead, configure the ``junit_duration_report`` option like this:
         [pytest]
         junit_duration_report = call
 
+Subtests are reported as separate ``testcase`` elements, alongside their parent
+test. Each subtest name contains the parent name, a one-based execution index
+(for example, ``test_example [subtest 1]``), and its message and parameters.
+The index distinguishes repeated subtest contexts and restarts for each parent
+execution. Both passing and unsuccessful subtests appear in the XML.
+
+Suite counts include the parent and every subtest. The parent keeps its own
+reported outcome, including any failure caused by failed subtests, so both the
+parent and a subtest can count as failures. Each subtest reports its own call
+duration; the parent retains its inclusive duration according to
+``junit_duration_report``. These times overlap and should not be added together.
+Subtest durations from ``unittest.TestCase.subTest`` are currently reported as
+zero, as supplied by the unittest integration.
+
